newsitem.title: USA: U.S Jan consumer credit grew $8.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S Jan consumer credit grew $8.4 billion.

text.p: U.S. consumer installment credit rose in January by $8.4 billiion at an 8.4 percent annual rate, the Federal Reserve said on Friday, more than double the revised $3.8 billion increase in December at a 3.9 percent rate.
It was the largest monthly increase in total consumer credit since a matching $8.4-billion rise in August last year.

Revolving, or credit-card credit, shot up by $7.9 billion at a 20.6 percent annual rate in January -- the biggest monthly increse in 16 months, the Fed said. Credit-card debt had risen only $2 billion at a 5.2 percent rate in December.
Previously, the Fed said December consumer credit had increased by $4.9 billion.
Auto credit outstanding grew in January by $1.3 billion at a 3.8 percent annual rate after rising in December by $600 million at a 2.2 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes and to pay for education but not real estate mortgages, fell by $700 million at a 2.6 percent annual rate in January. In December, this category of credit rose $1.1 billion at a 3.9 percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in January was $1.21 trillion, up from $1.12 trillion a year earlier.
